prerequisites.description: Active Asana account with access to a test workspace.
prerequisites.whyNeeded: Required to access Asana developer console and create OAuth client credentials.

steps.title: Access Asana Developer Dashboard
steps.purpose: Establish application identity and access developer credentials.
steps.whereToGo: https://app.asana.com/0/developer-console > "Asana App > Profile Avatar > Settings > Apps > Developer Console"
steps.instructions: Navigate to https://app.asana.com/0/developer-console. Sign in and go to: "Asana App > Profile Avatar > Settings > Apps > Developer Console".
steps.howToVerify: Confirm browser loads the developer dashboard at "Asana App > Profile Avatar > Settings > Apps > Developer Console".

steps.title: Register New OAuth Application in Asana
steps.purpose: Registers your client identity with the authorization server.
steps.instructions: Click "Developer Console > "+ New App"". Complete the registration form fields: App name, Workspace/Organization, Redirect URLs.
steps.expectedOutcome: Application created in developer console. Client ID is generated.
steps.howToVerify: Verify application entry appears in dashboard with generated Client ID.

steps.title: Configure Authorized Redirect URIs
steps.purpose: Prevents authorization code interception by locking callbacks to your server.
steps.instructions: In the redirect settings, enter your callback URL (e.g. "http://localhost:3000/api/auth/callback/asana"). Note rule: Must be HTTPS for production; http://localhost allowed for development.. Save changes.
steps.howToVerify: Confirm saved redirect URI appears under whitelisted callbacks with exact matching protocol.

steps.title: Select Permission Scopes & Secure Client Secret
steps.purpose: Configures granular API access permissions and obtains server credentials.
steps.instructions: Retrieve your Client ID and generate your Client Secret. Supported scopes: default (Inherits all project, task, and workspace access granted to the authorizing user.). Scope location rule: Asana uses default unified user-inherited permissions.. Store Client Secret in backend environment variables.
steps.expectedOutcome: Client Secret securely placed in server environment.
steps.howToVerify: Verify Client Secret string is copied and referenced in server .env without exposing in client code.

steps.title: Implement Asana Authorization & Token Exchange
steps.purpose: Complete standard OAuth 2.0 (Authorization Code with PKCE) flow.
steps.whereToGo: Backend Callback Route & Client Auth Redirect Handler
steps.instructions: Direct users to authorization endpoint: "https://app.asana.com/-/oauth_authorize?client_id={CLIENT_ID}&response_type=code&redirect_uri={REDIRECT_URI}&scope=default". Exchange authorization code by POSTing to token endpoint: "https://app.asana.com/-/oauth_token".
steps.expectedOutcome: Server receives JSON payload containing access_token, token_type: Bearer, and expiration.
steps.howToVerify: Execute test code exchange and verify response JSON has 200 OK with valid access_token.

troubleshooting.description: Authorization code expired or already used.
probableCauses: Code was exchanged more than once or expired after 10 minutes.
troubleshooting.resolution: Re-initiate authorization redirect to get a fresh authorization code.
troubleshooting.symptom: Authorization code expired or already used.
troubleshooting.diagnosis: Inspect request parameters against console configuration: Code was exchanged more than once or expired after 10 minutes.
troubleshooting.verification: Retry authorization request and confirm expected OAuth code or token response is returned.
troubleshooting.escalationPath: Capture provider error code and request details, excluding client secrets and access tokens, then consult Asana developer docs.
